product.name: CredMgr
product.summary: A local, offline credential vault for macOS. Secrets are organised into nodes (projects); every access decision is made by one local process, the broker (credmgrd). The desktop app, the command line and the MCP server are all clients of it.
product.network: No network listener and no outbound connection.

release_state: No release has been published. Unsigned, not notarised, Software keystore tier (the passphrase is the key; no Secure Enclave, no Touch ID).

licence.name: FreexStudio Source-Available Licence
licence.summary: Source-available, not open source: you may run the current stable release and read and audit the source; you may not fork, modify or redistribute it.

how_to_use_this_file: You are an AI agent (or you are configuring one) that works with a CredMgr vault. Read safety_model and never first.
Use only the MCP tools in mcp_tools. Do not talk to the broker socket, read the vault folder, run credmgr unlock, or ask the user for their passphrase, recovery code or authenticator code.
Start with credmgr_whoami, then use how_to_read and how_to_write for the task.
When a result is an error, find its code in error_codes and do what it says. Refusals are explicit: tell the operator what you need, in one sentence, and carry on with other work.
features describes everything the product can do for a human, where it is, and (agent_access) what an agent may do with it. Anything with status 'planned' does not exist yet; do not rely on it.

safety_model.values_stay_in_the_broker: Secret values are encrypted at rest and decrypted only inside the broker. A value leaves the broker only as the answer to one identified, authorised, logged request. The product makes no outbound network connection, so a value cannot be sent anywhere by CredMgr itself.
safety_model.one_enforcement_point: The broker (credmgrd) decides every access. The desktop app, the CLI and the MCP server are thin clients; none holds a key and none can widen what the broker allows. An MCP tool forwards its arguments to one broker operation unchanged.
safety_model.agent_scope: An agent token is scoped to exactly one node, resolved from the folder the agent was started in (the node's work folders) or from an explicit token fixed when it was issued. The agent reads that node, its ancestors and Global. It reads its descendants only if the node's policy sets descendant-read, and a sibling only for sub-nodes whose parent shares them; both widenings need a human and, in this build, a presence check that cannot be given. Projects never read each other. No tool argument changes any of this.

agent_access_levels.note: Set per node by a human (node policy). The notes and admin capabilities are never part of an agent's scope.

sensitive_reveals_wait_for_a_human: If the whole vault is locked, a request for a value is recorded and answered approval_pending. A person decides it with the passphrase (and the authenticator code when two-factor is on) on the Lock screen or with `credmgr approve`; approval covers one request, one entry, once, and expires after 120 seconds. The vault stays locked.

If the node's policy requires a second factor (reveal or always) and the vault has one enrolled, an agent gets two_factor_required until a person proves the factor. One code opens a vault-wide window of five minutes. The owner's own login is not asked.
A value is never staged for one caller and handed to another: an approval is one slot per (node, entry, requester) and releases only the fields that request asked for.

writes.create_while_locked: credmgr_create works on a locked vault. The entry is not written to the manifest: it is held in a review tray and a person accepts or discards it. Say so to the operator.
writes.update_needs_unlocked: credmgr_update, credmgr_rotate, credmgr_remove, credmgr_undo and the three field tools need the vault and node unlocked, because overwriting a credential you cannot read would be credential substitution.
writes.generation_check: Every change to an existing entry carries its current generation. A concurrent change answers conflict; re-read and retry once.
writes.undo: Rotations, field changes and removals are undoable by audit record id. A removal and a field change can be undone for seven days; a rotation has no time limit. Undo is itself audited.

safety_model.audit: Every decision, allowed or denied, is recorded in a hash-chained log. An agent can read only a redacted feed (id, action, time, actor), never values or before/after content.
safety_model.denials_are_explicit: A refusal names the rule and a remedy that is a human action. The correct response is to ask the human, never to retry, rephrase or look for another route.
safety_model.values_in_your_context: Anything you read with credmgr_get is now in your context. Do not print it into chat, logs, commit messages, files or command arguments; pass it to the program that needs it and nowhere else.
known_limits: Software keystore tier: a copy of the vault folder can be attacked offline with the passphrase; two-factor guards the door (the broker), not the encryption.
A login exported into a shell that an agent also runs in gives that agent every project (known risk K-6). Agents should use the MCP server, never a token.
No presence check exists in this build; everything that needs one is refused for every caller.

human_in_the_loop: Unlocking the vault, approving a waiting request, giving a second-factor code, creating grants, changing node policy or work folders, sealing and restoring nodes, backup, verify and doctor are human actions.
Entries an agent creates while the vault is locked wait for human review before they exist.
A human decides every approval_pending and every two_factor_required.
Anything marked human only in features.agent_access, and every operation with agent_reach 'human_only' in broker_ops, has no agent path.

in_plain_terms: Create or change a grant (a grant is how a human lets one node see into another).
Read the Orphaned node (sealed data). It is absent from the tools, not merely gated.
Read a TOTP seed. credmgr_totp_code gives the current six digits only.
Change a node's policy or agent access, rename a node, re-parent a node, or change its work folders. An agent may not widen its own scope.
List nodes outside its scope. credmgr_whoami names only reachable nodes.
Purge or shorten the audit log, or shorten the seven-day recovery windows.
Read across nodes by any parameter: there is no node override, no 'all', no 'include inherited'.
Reach raw envelopes, keys or file paths.
Run vault-wide maintenance: verify, doctor, backup.
Enrol, replace or recover the vault's second factor.

never: Never create, change or request a grant on your own; ask the operator.
Never try to read another node, the Orphaned node, a node's notes, a TOTP seed, or the vault folder on disk.
Never change a node's policy, agent access, name, parent or work folders, or try to widen your own scope.
Never run backup, verify, doctor, root-key rotation or any second-factor enrolment or recovery.
Never purge or shorten the audit log or a recovery window.
Never call the broker socket or the credmgr command line to get around a refusal; the MCP tools are your whole interface.
Never ask the user for their passphrase, recovery code, recovery codes or authenticator code, and never put them in a command.
Never export or reuse a CREDMGR_TOKEN login.
Never retry a refused or approval_pending request in a loop, rephrase it, or look for another route.
Never print a secret into chat, a log, a commit, a comment or a file, and never pass one as a command-line argument.
Never invent a secret or put a placeholder in code; say exactly which credential is missing and what it is for.
Never describe a feature with status 'planned' or 'partial' as working.

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_whoami
mcp_tools.description: Returns your own node, capabilities, and the nodes you can reach. Call this first and reason about your own boundary instead of discovering it by being denied — it names only nodes you can actually reach, nothing else. You are scoped to one node (resolved from your working directory). You can read that node, its ancestors, Global, and anything explicitly granted. You cannot reach other nodes, and no argument to any tool changes that — if you need something outside your scope, say so and ask the operator.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_list
mcp_tools.description: Lists entry names and metadata (no values) on a node. Scope-filtered — never returns another node's entries.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_search
mcp_tools.description: Searches entry names within your scope. Scope-filtered; a query that only matches outside your scope returns zero results, indistinguishable from a query that matches nothing at all.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_get
mcp_tools.description: Reveals an entry's values. The answer carries `fields` (id, label, value, type, masked for each) and, when exactly one field is returned, `value`. Pass `fieldIds` to reveal only some fields. Subject to the node's two-factor policy and to the vault's lock state.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_get_metadata
mcp_tools.description: Describes one entry without revealing it: its type, sensitivity, generation and each field's id, label, type and masking — never a value. Use it to find the field ids the other tools take. Needs the vault and node unlocked (labels are encrypted with the values).
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_create
mcp_tools.description: Creates a new entry (a name not already present on the node): one `value`, or a `fields` array of {label, value} objects for several fields. Send structure — the broker does not parse `label: value` text. Works on a locked vault — lands in the pending tray for human review at next unlock.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_update
mcp_tools.description: Modifies an existing entry: `value` replaces one field's value (name the field with `field` when the entry has several), `fields` replaces the whole list. Requires the vault unlocked — a locked-vault write-without-read-first would be credential substitution, not an update.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_rotate
mcp_tools.description: Replaces an entry's value (or its fields) and preserves the previous ciphertext as history. Takes the same body as credmgr_update. Requires the vault unlocked — same policy gate as credmgr_update: a legitimate rotation implies you could have read what you are replacing.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_field_add
mcp_tools.description: Adds fields to an entry (appended, or inserted at `position`) — it never replaces what is there. The previous state is retained; credmgr_undo reverses it. Requires the vault unlocked.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_field_update
mcp_tools.description: Changes one field — its label, its value, its type or its masking (`"auto"` goes back to inferring a type or masking). The previous state is retained; credmgr_undo reverses it. Requires the vault unlocked.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_field_remove
mcp_tools.description: Removes one field from an entry; the last field cannot be removed (remove the entry instead). The previous state is retained; credmgr_undo reverses it. Requires the vault unlocked.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_remove
mcp_tools.description: Soft-deletes an entry into a 7-day recovery window. Requires the vault unlocked. The entry stops appearing in credmgr_list/credmgr_search immediately; a human can recover it within the window.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_undo
mcp_tools.description: Undoes a rotate, a field change or a removal, addressed by its audit record id (from credmgr_recent_changes) — never by guessing at what changed. Requires the vault unlocked. A removal's undo is only possible within its 7-day recovery window; a rotation's undo has no time limit. This is itself a new, audited action — the original record is never erased or rewritten.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_write: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_totp_code
mcp_tools.description: Returns the current 6-digit code for a stored TOTP item. On an entry with several fields, name the seed's field with `field` unless exactly one field is a TOTP seed. Never returns the seed itself — there is no tool that does; a leaked code is worth 30 seconds, a leaked seed is worth forever.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

mcp_tools.name: credmgr_recent_changes
mcp_tools.description: Redacted feed of recent decisions (allow and deny) — id, action, timestamp, actor. Never before/after values, and never the fields an agent caller cannot have (node, decision, detail): the underlying op is always redacted for an agent origin, not merely by this tool's own choice.
mcp_tools.input_schema: see how_to_read: the schema is given once, beside the task

error_codes.what_to_do: Stop. The remedy field names the human action that would allow it (usually a grant). Tell the operator what you need and why in one sentence, and carry on with other work. Do not retry or rephrase.

The node asks for a second factor and none is in force. A person must give a code (an elevation lasts five minutes for the whole vault). Ask the operator, then retry once after they confirm. Do not ask for the code yourself.

The vault is locked and the operator has been asked. The request id and the seconds left are in the answer. Wait or do other work; a person decides with the passphrase. Retry the identical request after they say they decided, within 120 seconds. Do not poll in a loop.
Someone changed the entry first. Read it again (credmgr_get_metadata for the new generation), re-apply the change and retry once.
The whole vault is locked. Only entry creation (held for review) is allowed. Do other work or ask the operator to unlock; do not retry in a loop.
The vault is unlocked but this one node is locked. Ask the operator to unlock the node; the remedy field says how.
Not an agent concern: unlock is a human step. Tell the operator.
Fix the request. The message names the problem (an index or field id, never a value). Check the tool's input schema.
Your scope does not carry this capability. Stop and ask the operator; no argument changes it.
No such node, entry, field or request. Check ids with credmgr_list and credmgr_get_metadata.
That name is already used on the node, or is a look-alike of one that is. Choose another name or update the existing entry.
A local failure outside the documented errors. Do not retry in a loop; tell the operator.
This needs a live presence check that no client of this build can give. Nothing can be done here; tell the operator it is a human, native-app action.
The seven-day restore window of a sealed node has passed. Terminal; tell the operator.
The operator denied the request, it expired after 120 seconds, or the vault locked after it was approved. Do not retry unprompted; ask the operator whether to ask again.
Too many wrong attempts. retryAfterSeconds says how long to wait. Do not retry in a loop.
A code was wrong, replayed, expired or already used; the broker does not say which. Stop and tell the operator.
No second-factor enrolment is in progress. A human step; tell the operator.
The seven-day recovery window of a removed entry has passed. Terminal.
That audit record cannot be undone (wrong action, denied, or too old). Nothing to do.
A vault already exists. Not an agent concern.
The vault folder is inside a git working tree and is refused. Not an agent concern.
No vault creation is in progress. Not an agent concern.
The retyped recovery code did not match. Not an agent concern.
The token presented is not a live login. Do not retry with it. An agent using MCP should not hold a token; tell the operator.

broker_op_reach_meaning.mcp: Exposed as an MCP tool. This is the agent's whole interface.
broker_op_reach_meaning.capability_only: No MCP tool. The broker would accept the call from an agent-origin client that holds the capability, so an agent must not use it: several are the human's review or maintenance steps.
broker_op_reach_meaning.human_only: Needs Admin, the owner's login, the notes capability or presence, which an agent scope never carries.
broker_op_reach_meaning.bootstrap: Vault creation, unlock and lock operations that any local process may send and an agent never needs.

agent_access_meaning.none: No agent path. The feature is part of the app or the command line and an agent has no tool for it, or it is not relevant to an agent.
agent_access_meaning.read-only metadata: An agent can use it through an MCP tool to learn names, ids, labels, types, counts or its own boundary. No secret value is returned.
agent_access_meaning.read with approval: An agent can ask for secret values through an MCP tool. The broker answers at once only when the vault and node are unlocked and the node asks for no second factor; otherwise the request waits for a human (approval_pending or two_factor_required).
agent_access_meaning.read-write within its node: An agent can create or change data through an MCP tool, only inside the node it is scoped to, subject to that node's agent-access policy. Changes are audited, generation-checked and undoable.
agent_access_meaning.human only: Only a person can do this. An agent has no tool for it and the broker refuses an agent-origin caller.

features.title: Create the vault: choose a passphrase
features.summary: The first time the app starts with no vault, it asks you to choose a passphrase (step 1 of 4). The passphrase opens the vault on this machine; nothing is created anywhere else. Nothing in this version can recover a lost passphrase.
features.where: App: first run, step 1 of 4. CLI: credmgr init
steps: Type a passphrase of at least 4 characters (8 or more is recommended).

features.title: Recovery code, shown once
features.summary: Step 2 shows a 256-bit root recovery code once. Together with your passphrase it resets the second factor if you lose your authenticator. Write it on paper and keep it away from the passphrase. Retyping it is optional in the app; the CLI requires the retype before it writes anything.
features.where: App: first run, step 2 of 4. CLI: credmgr init (retype when asked)
steps: Optionally retype it to prove you have it, or skip.

features.title: Optional second factor at first run
features.summary: Step 3 offers to set up a second factor (an authenticator app). The QR code is drawn inside the window and nothing is sent anywhere. After you confirm one code, ten one-time recovery codes are shown once. You may skip it and enrol later in Settings; until you do, the vault rests on the passphrase alone.
features.where: App: first run, step 3 of 4 (Enrol later to skip)
steps: Scan the QR code, or type the key by hand.
Save the ten recovery codes, then continue.

features.title: Name your first projects
features.summary: Step 4 creates up to three starting projects. Global is created automatically, and so is the Orphaned node that sealing needs. Each project is its own boundary: what is stored in one is invisible to the others. A new vault starts empty; nothing is imported.
features.where: App: first run, step 4 of 4
steps: Type up to three project names, or leave them blank.
Finish. You land on the graph.

features.title: The broker is not running
features.summary: If the app shows 'credmgr cannot reach its broker', the credmgrd process is not running or its socket is not where the app looks. Start credmgrd in a terminal or let launchd keep it running, then choose Retry. Nothing from the last session is shown.
features.where: App: startup screen. Terminal: credmgrd
steps: Run credmgrd, or install the launchd unit from the release package.

features.title: Unlock with your passphrase
features.summary: The Lock screen asks for the passphrase. Wrong tries count toward a back-off that grows with each failure; while backed off, the broker answers rate_limited with the seconds to wait.
features.where: App: Lock screen > passphrase. CLI: credmgr unlock
steps: If two-factor is on, the screen asks for a code next.
features.area_title: Unlocking, locking and the menu-bar icon

features.title: Unlock with a second-factor code
features.summary: When the vault has a second factor, unlocking asks for the 6 digits from your authenticator, or one of your ten recovery codes (each works once). On the command line, credmgr unlock answers two_factor_required and credmgr gate verify completes it.
features.where: App: Lock screen > 2FA code. CLI: credmgr gate verify <code>
steps: Enter the 6-digit code or a recovery code.
features.area_title: Unlocking, locking and the menu-bar icon

features.title: Lock the vault now
features.summary: Locking ends every login, clears a copied secret from the clipboard and returns the app to the Lock screen. It works from anywhere, including while typing or with a dialog open.
features.where: App: header lock chip, vault menu > Lock vault, or the shortcut Cmd+L. CLI: credmgr lock
steps: Press Cmd+L, or choose the 'unlocked' chip in the header.
features.area_title: Unlocking, locking and the menu-bar icon

features.title: Auto-lock after idle time
features.summary: The app locks itself after a period with no activity: 5, 15 or 60 minutes, or never (the setting warns). Even when set to never, the broker still locks on its own idle timer (15 minutes by default). Hiding the window also locks when auto-lock is on.
features.where: App: Settings > Security > Auto-lock
steps: Open Settings (the gear in the header).
features.area_title: Unlocking, locking and the menu-bar icon

features.title: Lock on sleep, screen lock and window close
features.summary: The desktop app locks the vault when the Mac sleeps, when the screen locks, when another user session takes over, and when you close the window. The Lock screen says why it locked. A daemon running without the app does not do this.
features.where: App: automatic. Menu-bar icon > Lock vault locks on demand
steps: Nothing to do; it happens by itself.
The Lock screen shows a note such as 'Locked because this Mac went to sleep.'
features.area_title: Unlocking, locking and the menu-bar icon

features.title: Lock a single node
features.summary: A node can be locked on its own while the vault stays unlocked. Names and types stay visible but values need the node unlocked. A node's policy can lock it after a number of idle seconds.
features.where: App: node right-click or the three-dot menu > Lock now / Unlock node; inspector > Unlock node. CLI: node policy --lock-after-seconds
steps: Right-click the node, choose Lock now.
To reopen it, choose Unlock node.
features.area_title: Unlocking, locking and the menu-bar icon

features.title: Unlock a single node
features.summary: Reopens a node that was locked on its own (by hand or by its idle timer) without touching the rest of the vault. Names and types are visible while it is locked; values and field labels need it unlocked. If a node says it is locked, this is the fix. There is no CLI command for it yet; use the app.
features.where: App: node menu > Unlock node; inspector > Unlock node
steps: Right-click the node, choose Unlock node.
features.area_title: Unlocking, locking and the menu-bar icon

features.title: The graph
features.summary: The main view draws your nodes as a graph. A filled circle is global, a ringed circle a project, a thinner ring a sub-node, a dashed ring the Orphaned node. Small dots around a node are its entries; their colour is a hash of the entry id, never a name or value. You can drag nodes to arrange them; positions are remembered on this device under hashed ids.
features.where: App: main area, graph mode (the 'graph' button in the left rail)
steps: Click a node to select it and open the inspector.
Drag a node to move it.
Press F to fit the graph to the window.

features.title: Hover cards
features.summary: Hovering a node shows how many entries it holds and how many of them are authenticator seeds. Hovering an entry dot shows its entry type. Nothing about names or values.
features.where: App: hover over a node or an entry dot on the graph

features.title: The tree view
features.summary: The tree is a full keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible peer to the graph, with the same information and the same node menu. It is not a fallback.
features.where: App: 'tree' button in the left rail, or press T
steps: Press T to switch between graph and tree.
Use the three-dot button on a row for the node menu.

features.title: The left rail
features.summary: The rail lists every node with its badges and entry count, plus the Orphaned node. On a narrow window it is hidden behind the menu button (three lines) in the header. Right-click a row for the node menu.
features.where: App: left rail (the menu button opens it on a narrow window)
steps: Click a row to select the node.
Right-click a row for Open, New entry, Rename, Lock and more.

features.title: The node menu
features.summary: Right-clicking a node (or the three-dot button in the tree) offers Open, New entry, New project or New sub-node, Grant access, Rename, Lock now or Unlock node, and Remove node. Global has no Rename or Remove. The Orphaned node only offers Open.
features.where: App: right-click a node in the graph or rail; three-dot button in the tree

features.title: Search
features.summary: The header search box finds node names in the page and entry names through the broker's search. It matches names only: field labels and values are never searched. It shows up to nine rows and says how many more there are. With an empty box it offers 'Add new' and, in Pro mode, recent nodes.
features.where: App: header search box, or press / to focus it. CLI: credmgr search <term>
steps: Press / (or click the box) and type.
Choose a row to select the node or open the entry.

features.title: Entries: all nodes or selected only
features.summary: The graph can show every node's entry dots at once or only the selected node's. The choice is remembered.
features.where: App: button at the top of the graph, or press E

features.title: The Orphaned node
features.summary: Orphaned holds sealed items. Names stay visible; the values are human-only and this build cannot open them, because that needs a presence check (Touch ID) it cannot make yet. The open button asks the broker and is refused.
features.where: App: left rail > orphaned, or vault menu > Orphaned

features.title: Create a project
features.summary: A project is a boundary: it has its own key, notes and agent scope, and projects never read each other. The dialog takes a name, a parent and optional work folders. In Pro mode an advanced block sets agent access, second-factor requirement, hidden name and sibling sharing at creation.
features.where: App: right-click global > New project; Settings > Nodes > + New project (Pro); the empty-graph button. CLI: credmgr node create
steps: Open the dialog from one of the places above.
Pick the parent: global makes a project.

features.title: Create a sub-node
features.summary: A sub-node lives under a project. The tree stops at two levels, so a sub-node cannot have children.
features.where: App: right-click a project > New sub-node
steps: Name it and choose Create node.

features.title: Work folders: scope an agent to a node
features.summary: Binding folders to a node means any process started inside one of them, such as an AI coding agent, is scoped to that node automatically: it can read the node and its ancestors, never another project. The longest matching folder wins. An agent started outside every bound folder sees only that the vault exists.
features.where: App: New node dialog > work folders. CLI: credmgr node workdir <id> <dir>...
steps: Add a folder when creating the node, or run credmgr node workdir <id> <dir>.
Run credmgr node workdir <id> with no folder to clear the list.

features.title: Rename a node
features.summary: Renaming changes the display name only; the node id never changes. Global cannot be renamed.
features.where: App: right-click a node > Rename, then Enter or click away. CLI: credmgr node rename
steps: Choose Rename, type the new name, press Enter. Esc cancels.

features.title: Node policy: agent access
features.summary: Sets what an agent scoped to this node may do: read-write (list, read metadata, reveal, create, update), read-only (list, read metadata, reveal) or none. In the app it is chosen when the node is created (Pro mode); change it later with the CLI.
features.where: App: New node dialog > advanced (Pro). CLI: credmgr node policy

features.title: Node policy: require a second factor
features.summary: With a vault second factor set up, a node can ask callers other than you for a fresh code: 'reveal' asks before a value leaves the vault, 'always' asks before any read of the node. Your own login is not asked. The factor and the five-minute window belong to the whole vault, not to one node.
features.where: App: New node dialog > advanced (Pro); the node shows a chip when it is set. CLI: credmgr node policy --require-two-factor

features.title: Node policy: hide the node's name
features.summary: A node with hidden names shows other callers an opaque row instead of its label, entry names and notes. The node id is opaque and fixed when the node is created.
features.where: App: New node dialog > 'Hide this node's name' (Pro). CLI: credmgr node policy --private-names
steps: Tick the option when creating the node, or run credmgr node policy <id> --reason "why" --private-names.

features.title: Node policy: sibling and descendant reading
features.summary: Two options widen who can read: sub-nodes seeing each other (siblings shared) and a node reading its children. Turning either off is immediate. Turning either on needs a presence check this build cannot make, so the broker refuses and applies nothing.
features.where: CLI: credmgr node policy --sibling-visibility, --descendant-read
steps: Run credmgr node policy with --sibling-visibility isolated or --no-descendant-read to narrow.

features.title: Node policy: lock a node after idle seconds
features.summary: A node can carry its own idle timer. When it runs out the node locks while the vault stays open.
features.where: CLI: credmgr node policy --lock-after-seconds <n>|none

features.title: Node notes
features.summary: Each node can hold one markdown note, sealed under the node's key. The inspector shows it. Writing a note is a CLI action; an empty input is refused so a failed pipe cannot erase a note, and 'notes clear' is the only deletion. Agents never hold the notes capability.
features.where: App: inspector > notes (read). CLI: credmgr notes show | set | clear

features.title: Write or clear a node note
features.summary: Notes are written on the command line: credmgr notes set takes the text from a file or stdin and refuses empty input, and credmgr notes clear is the only way to delete one. The desktop app shows a note but has no editor for it.
features.where: CLI: credmgr notes set <id> [--file <path>], credmgr notes clear <id>

features.title: Move a node under a different parent
features.summary: Re-parenting changes which nodes can read a node, which is a grant by another name, so it needs presence. The operation exists and refuses everyone in this build.
features.where: No control in the app or CLI

features.title: Add an entry
features.summary: An entry is one named secret that can hold any number of fields, each with a label you choose. The dialog asks where (which node), a name (up to 200 characters), and either a single set of fields or a bulk paste. A preview shows exactly what will be stored; nothing is written until you save. If the node or vault is locked the entry is held for review instead (see Writes made while locked).
features.where: App: inspector > + New entry, press N, node menu > New entry, or search > Add new. CLI: credmgr set <name> --node <id>
steps: Pick the node and type a name.
Enter label and value, or switch to Bulk.
Check the preview, then choose Save (or Save and add another).

features.title: Bulk paste: one entry from many lines
features.summary: Bulk mode takes a paste of 'label: value' lines (a colon followed by a space) and turns it into one entry with one field per line. A line of three slashes separates blocks, so a value can span lines, such as a private key. A box can split each slash-separated block into its own entry. The preview shows the result before you save.
features.where: App: Add entry dialog > Bulk. CLI: credmgr set <name> --node <id> --bulk
steps: Check the preview, optionally tick 'split each /// segment into its own entry', then save.

features.title: Entry type and sensitivity
features.summary: Every entry has a type (server, database, api, wallet, login, ssh, certificate, token, totp, env-bundle, note or other) and a sensitivity (low, medium, high, critical). Both are inferred from the fields and can be pinned; 'auto' returns to inferring. A seed phrase or private key raises sensitivity to critical.
features.where: App: Add entry dialog > entry type; preview shows the inferred sensitivity
steps: Leave 'auto', or pick a type in the entry type list.

features.title: Add a note (free-text entry)
features.summary: A note is an entry whose single value is free text, for anything that is not a credential. It is audited like any entry. It is different from the node note, which is one markdown page per node.
features.where: App: inspector > + New note

features.title: List the entries of a node
features.summary: The inspector lists a node's entries with their type and a 2FA badge. A node you cannot read, or one that is locked, says so instead of showing an empty list.
features.where: App: select a node; inspector on the right. CLI: credmgr list [--node <id>]

features.title: Open an entry and see its fields
features.summary: Opening an entry shows its fields: label, type, and a masked value. The broker answers with field ids, labels, types and masking and never a value; values appear only when you reveal or copy one. Labels are encrypted with the values, so a locked node shows only names and types.
features.where: App: click an entry in the inspector. CLI: credmgr field ls <name>
steps: Use the back arrow to return to the node.

features.title: Replace a value
features.summary: Replaces one field's value, or the whole field list, in place. It keeps no history. Use rotate when the old value should be kept.
features.where: CLI: credmgr set <name> --node <id> --field <label>. App: field menu > Edit
steps: Pipe the new value on stdin: credmgr set vps --node acme --field password.

features.title: Rotate a secret and keep history
features.summary: Rotation replaces the value and keeps the previous one as history, so it can be undone with no time limit. A legitimate rotation implies you could have read what you replace, so it needs the vault unlocked.
features.where: CLI: credmgr rotate <name>
steps: Pipe the new value on stdin: credmgr rotate API_KEY --node acme.

features.title: Remove an entry (soft delete)
features.summary: Removing hides the entry from lists and search at once and keeps it for seven days, when undo can bring it back. The desktop app has no control for this yet; use the CLI.
features.where: CLI: credmgr rm <name>. App: no control
steps: To bring it back inside seven days, run credmgr undo <audit id> --node <id>.

features.title: Undo a change
features.summary: Undo reverses a rotation, a field change or a removal, addressed by the audit record id. A removal can be undone for seven days and a field change for seven days; a rotation has no limit. In the app the inspector shows 'Undo' for the most recent change on the node while nothing else has changed it. Undo is itself an audited action.
features.where: App: inspector > Undo button under the fields. CLI: credmgr undo <audit id> --node <id>
steps: Find the id with credmgr audit, then run credmgr undo <id> --node <node>.
If the name was reused, add --mode keep-both.

features.title: Generate a password
features.summary: The broker can generate a random password of 8 to 128 characters, with symbols on or off, or a pronounceable form, and tells you its strength. The value appears in the answer only; it is not stored or audited until you save it in a field.
features.where: App: Add field dialog > Generate. CLI: credmgr generate
steps: Choose Generate, then save the field.

features.title: Entry and node name rules
features.summary: Names are compared in one canonical form, so a look-alike of an existing name (different case, width, invisible characters or look-alike letters) is refused as already existing, for agents too. A name that mixes Latin with Greek or Cyrillic letters is accepted with a warning. Entry names are at most 200 characters; node labels 1 to 120.
features.where: Applies wherever a name is typed
steps: Choose a different name if you see 'already exists'.

features.title: Add a field
features.summary: Adds one or more fields to an entry, appended or inserted at a position. The label is free text and may be empty; there are no fixed field names. The type and whether it is hidden are inferred from the label and value.
features.where: App: open an entry > + Add field. CLI: credmgr field add
steps: Type a label and a value (or Generate), then save.

features.title: Edit a field
features.summary: Changes a field's label, value, type or hidden state. The current value is never shown in the dialog; leave the new value empty to keep it. Only what you change is sent. The previous state is kept as history.
features.where: App: field three-dot menu > Edit. CLI: credmgr field set
steps: Open the field menu and choose Edit.
Change what you need and save.

features.title: Remove a field
features.summary: Removes one field from an entry. An entry keeps at least one field; remove the entry instead. Undoable.
features.where: App: field three-dot menu > Remove. CLI: credmgr field rm
steps: Open the field menu, choose Remove, confirm.

features.title: Reorder fields
features.summary: Moves a field up or down. Order is presentation only.
features.where: App: field three-dot menu > Move up / Move down. CLI: credmgr field mv
steps: Open the field menu and choose Move up or Move down.

features.title: Field types and hidden values
features.summary: A field has one of eleven types: password, api-key, private-key, seed-phrase, totp-seed, username, host, port, url, certificate, text. The type is inferred from label and value and can be pinned. Password, api-key, private-key, seed-phrase and totp-seed fields are hidden by default; any field can be pinned shown or hidden.
features.where: App: Add entry preview and Edit field dialog
steps: Pick a type in the preview list, or choose auto.

features.title: Reveal a value
features.summary: Reveal fetches one field's value and shows it for the reveal window (10, 20 or 60 seconds; 20 by default), then hides it again with a countdown. Each reveal is audited. An agent asking the broker for a value goes through the same gate: if the vault is locked the request waits for you; if the node asks for a second factor it needs a fresh code.
features.where: App: open an entry > Reveal on a field. CLI: credmgr get <name> --field <label>
steps: The value hides again when the countdown ends or you lock.

features.title: Copy a value without revealing it
features.summary: Copy places the value on the clipboard through the app's native shell and never passes it through the window. The clipboard is cleared after 30 seconds and when the vault locks. Every copy is audited.
features.where: App: field row > Copy

features.title: Read a value on the command line
features.summary: credmgr get prints one value on stdout. An entry with several fields needs a selector (--field, --field-id) or --all; without one it exits 2 and lists the labels. --json prints the fields.
features.where: CLI: credmgr get

features.title: Conflict protection on writes
features.summary: Every change to an existing entry carries the entry's current generation. If something else changed it first, the broker answers conflict with both generations and nothing is applied. Re-read, re-apply, retry once.
features.where: Automatic
steps: On a conflict, read the entry again and repeat the change.

features.title: Store an authenticator seed
features.summary: A field holding an otpauth URI, a base32 secret of a standard length (16, 20, 24, 26, 32, 40, 52, 56 or 64 characters, upper case or in groups of four), or a field typed totp-seed is a stored authenticator seed. The entry gets a 2FA badge and counts toward the node's 2FA number. This is separate from the vault's own second factor.
features.where: App: Add entry with a seed field. CLI: credmgr set <name> --node <id>
steps: Add a field whose value is the seed.

features.title: Show the current 6-digit code
features.summary: Revealing a seed field shows the current 6-digit code with a bar that runs to the end of its 30-second step. The seed itself is never shown or returned: a reveal of a seed field answers with the value removed. Codes use SHA-1, 6 digits, 30 seconds.
features.where: App: seed field > Reveal. CLI: none. MCP: credmgr_totp_code
steps: Choose Reveal on the seed field.

features.title: Show the seed itself
features.summary: Not available. A code is worth thirty seconds, a seed is worth forever, so reading it needs a presence check this build cannot make. The 'show seed' button asks the broker and is refused.
features.where: App: seed field > show seed (refused)

features.title: Set up or replace the second factor
features.summary: Enrolling gives the vault a second factor: the broker will not unlock without a fresh code from your authenticator. The QR code is drawn locally. After you confirm one code, ten recovery codes are shown once. Replacing a confirmed factor needs a fresh code from the current one first (unlock again, then do it within five minutes).
features.where: App: Settings > Security > Two-factor gate. CLI: credmgr gate enroll
steps: Scan the QR code and enter one code.

features.title: Lost your authenticator
features.summary: The passphrase, plus the root recovery code printed when the vault was created, resets the second factor. It does not unlock: unlock afterwards, then enrol a new authenticator. Without both, nothing recovers it.
features.where: App: Lock screen > 'lost your authenticator?'. CLI: credmgr gate recover
steps: Enter the passphrase and the root recovery code.
Choose Reset and unlock, then enrol again.

features.title: The ten recovery codes
features.summary: Enrolment issues ten one-time codes, each good once in place of an authenticator code at unlock. They are shown once and cannot be shown again. They are not the root recovery code.
features.where: App: after confirming a code; the Lock screen accepts one in the 2FA field
steps: Store them apart from the passphrase.

features.title: Give the second factor to agents
features.summary: For nodes whose policy asks for a second factor, an agent or tool gets two_factor_required until a person proves the factor. One code opens a vault-wide window of five minutes in which agents and other tools pass the gate on every node that asks. A lock or any node policy change ends it. Your own login is never asked.
features.where: App: 'Give second factor' on the node chip or in the inspector. CLI: credmgr gate verify <code> in a shell that holds your login
steps: Choose Give second factor on the node.

features.title: What the second factor does and does not protect
features.summary: The check is made by credmgrd, not by the encryption. Anyone who has your passphrase or your recovery code and a copy of the vault folder can decrypt it without the second factor. Treat each of the passphrase and the recovery code as a complete key.
features.where: Applies to the whole vault
steps: Keep the passphrase and recovery code offline and apart.

features.title: Decide an agent's waiting request
features.summary: If an agent asks for a value while the whole vault is locked, the broker records the request and answers approval_pending. You decide it while the vault stays locked: you give the passphrase (and the authenticator code if two-factor is on). Approving decrypts that one entry and hands it to the agent's retry once; the vault stays locked. A request expires and is denied after 120 seconds.
features.where: App: Lock screen > 'N agent requests are waiting for approval'. CLI: credmgr approvals, credmgr approve <request>
steps: Open the Lock screen's request list and pick a request.

features.title: See what a request asks for
features.summary: Before deciding, you can see what each waiting request is: the node, the entry (by name unless the node hides names), the command and the seconds left. The list works while locked and decrypts nothing. The Lock screen checks the waiting count every five seconds.
features.where: App: Lock screen request list. CLI: credmgr approvals [<request>]
steps: Run credmgr approvals, or open the request list on the Lock screen.

features.title: Writes made while locked are held for review
features.summary: An entry added while the vault or its node is locked does not enter the manifest. It waits in the pending tray, across restarts, showing node, name, field count, type, sensitivity and when it was held, and never its values. Accept writes it to its node; Discard removes it. Accepting needs the node unlocked.
features.where: App: header 'N held' chip, the banner after unlock (Review), or vault menu > Pending writes. CLI: credmgr pending
steps: Choose Accept or Discard on each row.

features.title: Accept or discard a held entry
features.summary: Each held entry is accepted or discarded on its own. A name already used on the node is refused rather than overwritten.
features.where: App: Held for review > Accept / Discard. CLI: credmgr pending accept|discard <entry> --node <id>

features.title: The review banner
features.summary: After you unlock, a banner reports how many held entries are waiting, with Review and dismiss buttons. The header chip stays until the tray is empty.
features.where: App: banner under the header after unlock

features.title: See and revoke grants
features.summary: A grant lets one node see into another. The list shows from and to, the scope (read, reveal, notes), a reason and when it ends. Revoking closes it at once in both Lite and Pro mode, because revoking is safety.
features.where: App: Settings > Grants > Revoke. CLI: credmgr grant ls, credmgr grant revoke <id>

features.title: List grants
features.summary: Shows every grant: from and to, scope, reason and when it ends. Grants made elsewhere appear here even though this build cannot create one.
features.where: App: Settings > Grants. CLI: credmgr grant ls
steps: Open Settings > Grants, or run credmgr grant ls.

features.title: Create a grant
features.summary: The dialog takes a from-node, a to-node, what to allow (read, reveal values, notes) and a reason of at least eight characters. In this build the broker refuses the request with presence_required, because creating a grant widens a boundary and needs a presence check nothing can make yet; nothing changes. Grants made elsewhere are listed and can be revoked. A grant never expires by itself.
features.where: App: node menu > Grant access; Settings > Grants > + New grant (Pro); drag one node onto another. CLI: credmgr grant <from> --to <node> --scope read --reason "..."
steps: The dialog validates your input, sends it, and shows the presence notice.

features.title: How isolation and grants work
features.summary: Projects never read each other. A node reads itself, Global and its ancestors. It reads its children only if its own policy allows it, and a sibling only for sub-nodes whose parent shares them. Anything else is a grant: human-only, with a reason, revocable, drawn as a dashed arrow on the graph from the trusted node to the node it can see into. An agent can never create one.
features.where: Concept; see the graph legend in Help
steps: Read the dashed arrows on the graph.

features.title: Remove (seal) a node
features.summary: Removing a node never deletes it. Its entries are re-encrypted to the Orphaned node's key, names stay visible and values become human-only. You type the node name to confirm. A node that still has sub-nodes cannot be sealed until they are sealed; Global cannot be sealed.
features.where: App: node menu > Remove node; Settings > Nodes > Remove (Pro). CLI: credmgr node seal <name>

features.title: Restore a sealed node
features.summary: A sealed node can be restored byte for byte for seven days, across restarts. After that restore is refused (archive_expired). Work folders another node has claimed since are not restored.
features.where: App: Settings > Nodes > Sealed nodes > Restore node (Pro). CLI: credmgr node restore <name>

features.title: The MCP server for AI agents
features.summary: credmgr mcp is a stdio MCP server that exposes 15 tools to an AI client. It forwards each call to the broker unchanged; the broker decides. You register it once, globally, in your AI client's MCP settings with the full path to the credmgr binary and the argument mcp. One entry serves every project because the folder the client starts in decides the node. Automatic setup of client config files does not exist yet.
features.where: AI client MCP settings (you edit them). CLI: credmgr mcp
steps: Add a server named credmgr: command = the full path to credmgr, args = ["mcp"].
Start the client inside a project folder bound to a node.
features.area_title: AI agents and the MCP server

features.title: An agent learns its own boundary
features.summary: credmgr_whoami returns the agent's node, its capabilities and the nodes it can reach, and names nothing else. An agent should call it first and reason about its own boundary instead of discovering it by being denied.
features.where: MCP: credmgr_whoami. CLI: credmgr whoami
features.area_title: AI agents and the MCP server

features.title: How an agent is scoped
features.summary: An agent is scoped to one node, resolved from the folder it was started in (the node's work folders), or from an explicit token. It reads that node, its ancestors and Global, plus anything granted. No tool argument changes that. An agent started in an unbound folder gets only a bare list on Global.
features.where: Set with work folders on a node
steps: Bind the project folder to the node (see Work folders).
features.area_title: AI agents and the MCP server

features.title: What each agent access level allows
features.summary: The node's agent access decides the agent's capabilities. read-write: list, read metadata, reveal, create, update. read-only: list, read metadata, reveal. none: nothing. The notes and admin capabilities are never part of an agent's scope, whatever the policy says.
features.where: CLI: credmgr node policy <id> --reason "..." --agent-access ...
steps: Choose the narrowest level that does the job.
features.area_title: AI agents and the MCP server

features.title: What an agent sees when the vault is locked
features.summary: Reading a value on a locked vault answers approval_pending and waits for you (see Decide an agent's waiting request); asking for an authenticator code on a locked vault is simply refused. Creating an entry works and lands in the pending tray for your review. Updating, rotating, removing and field changes are refused with vault_locked, because overwriting a credential you cannot read would be substitution.
features.where: Behaviour of the broker
steps: Agent: wait or carry on with other work; do not retry in a loop.
features.area_title: AI agents and the MCP server

features.title: What an agent does when refused
features.summary: A refusal is explicit and names the human action that would fix it in its remedy field. The right response is to say what is needed and why in one sentence, ask the operator, and carry on with other work. Do not retry, rephrase or look for another route.
features.where: Every MCP tool result that is an error
steps: Tell the operator what you need.
features.area_title: AI agents and the MCP server

features.title: What an agent can never do
features.summary: These are absent, not merely gated: create or change a grant; read the Orphaned node; read a stored authenticator seed (it can get the current 6-digit code); change a node's policy, agent access, name, parent or work folders; touch the second factor or recovery; run backup, verify, doctor or root-key rotation; purge or shorten the audit log or the recovery window; read another node under any argument; read notes. A test fails if a tool for any of these is added.
features.where: Enforced in the broker; restated in the MCP registry
features.area_title: AI agents and the MCP server

features.title: Private names and agents

steps: Set private names on a sensitive node.

It is generated from the same data as this help and is checked against the code, so it cannot silently drift.

steps: Give the file to an agent as context.

features.title: Keep your login out of an agent's shell
features.summary: credmgr unlock exports a login token that reaches every project until the vault locks or the token idles out for 15 minutes. Never export it into a shell an AI agent runs in: the agent would inherit your reach. Agents should use the MCP server, scoped by folder.
features.where: CLI: credmgr unlock; known risk K-6
steps: Unlock in a shell the agent cannot read, and lock when done.
features.area_title: AI agents and the MCP server

features.title: The credmgr command line
features.summary: One binary, credmgr, is the command line and the MCP server. A secret never travels as an argument: values come from stdin, so they stay out of shell history and process lists. --json gives machine output where offered. credmgr help lists every command and flag.
features.where: Terminal: credmgr help
steps: Pipe values: credmgr set API_KEY --node acme <<< 'value'.

features.title: Vault status
features.summary: Prints whether the vault is locked and, when there are any, how many agent requests are waiting.
features.where: CLI: credmgr status

features.title: Log in from a shell
features.summary: credmgr unlock reads the passphrase from stdin and prints an export line for CREDMGR_TOKEN; use eval to apply it. With two-factor on it answers two_factor_required and credmgr gate verify <code> completes it. credmgr lock ends every login.
features.where: CLI: credmgr unlock, credmgr lock

features.title: The broker: credmgrd
features.summary: credmgrd holds every key and makes every access decision. The app, the CLI and the MCP server are clients of its local socket and none holds a key. It speaks newline-delimited JSON over a Unix socket (mode 0600 in a 0700 folder), accepts only the vault owner's user id, and has no network listener and makes no outbound connection. Run it in a terminal or with the launchd unit in the release package.
features.where: Terminal: credmgrd; launchd unit packaging/com.credmgr.brokerd.plist
steps: Or copy the plist to ~/Library/LaunchAgents and bootstrap it.

features.title: Where the vault lives
features.summary: The vault folder is ~/Library/Application Support/credmgr (override with CREDMGR_VAULT_DIR) and must not be inside a git working tree. A rollback counter lives in ~/Library/Application Support/credmgr-state; moving a vault without it makes the first unlock refuse.
features.where: Filesystem
steps: Set CREDMGR_VAULT_DIR to use another location.
